chunks: As for what was narrated by Muḥammad ibn Aḥmad ibn Yaḥyā, from ʿImrān ibn Mūsā, from Muḥammad ibn ʿAbd al-Ḥamīd, from ʿAlī ibn al-Faḍl al-Wāsiṭī, who said:

I heard him saying: If the mutamattiʿ fasts two days and does not follow them with the fasting of the third day, then the fasting of three days during the hajj has escaped him. So let him fast in Makkah three consecutive days; and if he is not able, and the camel-driver does not remain for him, then let him fast them on the roads; or when he arrives to his family, he should fast ten consecutive days.

So this is not contrary to what we have mentioned, because it is not stated in the report which two days he fasted. Since that is not explicit in its outward wording, we interpret it as referring to one who did not fast on the Day of Tarwiyah and the Day of ʿArafah, but fasted two days after the Days of Tashrīq and did not add to them the third day; that is not permissible for him, because after the completion of the Days of Tashrīq, nothing is permissible except the fasting of three consecutive days. This is indicated by that.

key_terms.أَيَّامِ التَّشْرِيقِ: the Days of Tashrīq following Eid al-Aḍḥā
key_terms.الْجَمَّالُ: the camel-driver or transport handler with whom one travels
key_terms.صِيَامُ ثَلَاثَةِ أَيَّامٍ فِي الْحَجِّ: the required fasting of three days during the hajj
key_terms.عَشَرَةَ أَيَّامٍ: ten days of fasting as mentioned here upon returning to one's family
key_terms.يَوْمَ التَّرْوِيَةِ: the Day of Tarwiyah, a specific hajj date before ʿArafah

ai.seo_question: If a pilgrim in tamattuʿ fasts only two days and misses the third, what is the ruling?
ai.summary: This report discusses the legal ruling for the mutamattiʿ who must fast three days during hajj. It explains that after the Days of Tashrīq, these fasts must be performed as three consecutive days, and if the sequence is broken, the required hajj fasting is considered missed and other prescribed alternatives apply.
